places.name: Ghibli Park
places.connection: A theme park opened in 2022 featuring multiple areas based on Ghibli films, including Dondoko Forest, which is dedicated to My Neighbor Totoro.

places.name: Satsuki and Mei's House
places.connection: Full-scale recreation of the house from the film

places.name: Totoro's Forest No. 1
places.connection: The first plot of land purchased by the Totoro no Furusato Foundation (Totoro's Hometown Fund), a conservation effort started after the film's success to preserve the Sayama Hills.

places.name: Inari Shrine in Asagaya
places.connection: Some fan communities suggest this shrine, with its tree-lined path, may have inspired the sequence where Satsuki and Mei wait for the bus in the rain.

places.name: Studio Ghibli Headquarters
places.connection: The animation studio where 'My Neighbor Totoro' was created. While not open to the public, it is the birthplace of the film.

places.name: Sayama Hills (Totoro Forest)
places.connection: The primary inspiration for the film's setting. Miyazaki lives nearby and drew heavily from its landscapes.

places.name: Satsuki and Mei's House (Replica)
places.connection: A full-scale, meticulously detailed replica of the family's house, originally built for the 2005 World Expo and now a major attraction at Ghibli Park.

places.name: Ghibli Museum
places.connection: The official museum of Studio Ghibli, featuring exhibits on the animation process, a theater showing exclusive short films, and a giant Catbus for children to play in.

places.name: Shichikokuyama Hospital Site
places.connection: This hospital, which specialized in tuberculosis treatment, is widely believed to be the model for the one where the mother is recuperating.

places.name: Hachikokuyama Park
places.connection: One of the several parks within the Sayama Hills area that directly inspired the lush forests and rural scenery of the film.

places.name: Kurosuke's House (former location)
places.connection: A 1920s house that fans nicknamed 'Totoro's House' due to its resemblance to the film's aesthetic. It was preserved by the community but was destroyed in a fire in 2009. A small park remains.

places.name: Kurosuke's House (Soot Sprite House)
places.connection: Totoro Fund headquarters in preserved traditional house

places.name: Ghibli Park
places.connection: Theme park bringing Ghibli worlds to life

places.name: Totoro Forest (Sayama Hills)
places.connection: Inspiration for the forest setting; now protected land
